questions.s:

The student observed that the white anhydrous copper(II) sulfate turned blue and the purple acidified potassium manganate(VII) turned colourless.
Which gases were present in the gas sample?

2 filtration
3 sublimation
4 use of separating funnel

Which statement is correct?
o: A gaseous N molecule has a lower mass than a liquid N molecule.
Energy is released when N changes from liquid to solid.
Liquid N is at a higher temperature than solid N.
Liquid N molecules vibrate about fixed positions.

questions.s:
The cover plate was removed from the gas jars shown in the diagram. After several days, the colour of the gas was the same in both jars.
Which statement explains this change?
o: Oxygen and bromine gases have equal densities.
Oxygen and bromine molecules are in random motion.
Oxygen and bromine diffuse at the same rate.
Equal volumes of oxygen and bromine contain equal number of molecules.

questions.s:

Which substance has been wrongly classified as an element or mixture?
o: property: Black powder burns in air forming a colourless gas.; classification: element
property: Colourless solution produces two colourless gases when an electric current is passed through it.; classification: mixture

questions.s:
Hydrogen can form both H+ ions and H− ions.
Which statement about these two ions is correct?
o: A H<sup>+</sup> ion has no electron in its first shell.
A H<sup>+</sup> ion has more protons than an H<sup>−</sup> ion.
A H<sup>−</sup> ion has one more electron than an H<sup>+</sup> ion.
A H<sup>−</sup> ion is formed when a hydrogen atom loses an electron.

questions.s:
Toluene and cyclohexane are two common organic solvents and they form a homogenous mixture when mixed together.
The following graph shows the boiling points of mixtures containing different percentages of toluene and cyclohexane.
Which of the following best describes the boiling point of any mixture of toluene and cyclohexane as shown by the graph?
o: The boiling point is below that of cyclohexane.
The boiling point is higher than that of toluene.
The boiling point is below that of both toluene and cyclohexane.
The boiling point is between that of toluene and cyclohexane.
